name: colfer
workload: Marshal/unmarshal of a fixed struct (Name, BirthDay, Phone, Siblings, Spouse, Money) in the go_serialization_benchmarks shootout harness.
claimed_speedup: marshal 115 ns/op vs protobuf-go 287 ns/op (~2.5x), unmarshal 123 ns/op vs 356 ns/op (~2.9x); also far faster than msgpack (921/1216 ns/op) and capnproto (2181/364 ns/op) on marshal (derived from page data)
tradeoffs: Requires a schema-first IDL and code generation step; smaller ecosystem/tooling than protobuf; no reflection-based dynamic access.
caveats: Report page (report/data.js, rendered at alecthomas.github.io/go_serialization_benchmarks) does not state CPU model or Go compiler version, so capped at tier B despite the benchmark code being public and CI-run; numbers are for one struct shape only.
found_via: gh api repos/alecthomas/go_serialization_benchmarks/contents/report/data.js — go_serialization_benchmarks shootout results table

name: gencode
workload: Marshal/unmarshal of the same fixed struct used across the go_serialization_benchmarks harness.
claimed_speedup: marshal 122 ns/op (48 ns/op unsafe_reuse variant) vs protobuf-go 287 ns/op; unmarshal 132 ns/op (104 ns/op unsafe_reuse) vs 356 ns/op — roughly 2.3-6x faster (derived from page data)
tradeoffs: Codegen-based fixed schema; project has had no commits since 2018 so bug fixes/newer Go features are unlikely; copyleft (GPL-2.0) license may deter some integrations.
caveats: Same shared report page as other go_serialization_benchmarks entries: CPU model and Go compiler version not stated on the results page, capping tier at B; project itself is unmaintained (still valid as a fast algorithm/technique to study).

name: msgp
workload: Marshal/unmarshal of the same fixed struct used across the go_serialization_benchmarks harness, comparing msgp's codegen'd MessagePack implementation against the reflection-based vmihailenco/msgpack implementation of the same wire format.
claimed_speedup: marshal 134 ns/op vs msgpack (vmihailenco) 921 ns/op (~6.9x); unmarshal 200 ns/op vs 1216 ns/op (~6.1x); wire size slightly larger (97 vs 92 bytes) (derived from page data)
tradeoffs: Requires a `go generate` codegen step tied to struct tags; both implementations produce the same MessagePack wire format so this is a faster implementation of the baseline format rather than a different format beating it.
caveats: msgp and the compared vmihailenco/msgpack are both MessagePack implementations; the win is implementation speed, not a different wire format beating MessagePack. Report page does not state CPU/compiler, capping tier at B.

name: 200sc/bebop (Go)
workload: Marshal/unmarshal of the same fixed struct used across the go_serialization_benchmarks harness, using a Bebop-schema-generated Go codec.
claimed_speedup: marshal 94 ns/op (52 ns/op reuse) vs protobuf-go 287 ns/op (~3-5.5x); unmarshal 112 ns/op vs 356 ns/op (~3.2x); also far faster than capnproto (2181/364 ns/op) (derived from page data)
tradeoffs: Implements the Bebop IDL/wire format (a schema compiler is required); this is an independent third-party Go codegen backend, not the canonical Bebop repo, so cross-language support depends on this project tracking the Bebop spec.
caveats: This is a Go implementation of the Bebop format, distinct from the canonical https://github.com/6over3/bebop repo already catalogued (not a fork). Report page does not state CPU/compiler, capping tier at B.

name: bitcode
workload: Serialize/deserialize of the 'log' dataset (small HTTP-request-log-like structs with many strings) in djkoloski/rust_serialization_benchmark.
claimed_speedup: serialize 96.821 µs vs prost(protobuf) 731.23 µs (~7.6x), flatbuffers 763.63 µs (~7.9x), capnp 480.15 µs (~5.0x), rmp-serde(msgpack) 1.3179 ms (~13.6x); deserialize 1.1452 ms vs prost 2.6802 ms (~2.3x), rmp-serde 2.3829 ms (~2.1x); wire size 703,710 vs protobuf 884,628 bytes (derived from page data)
compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.100.0-nightly (a36d05efa, 2026-09-09); benchmarked via the repo's criterion-based harness, exact opt-level flags not itemized beyond the harness default
hardware: AMD EPYC 9V74 (2 cores / 4 threads visible to the VM), x86_64
tradeoffs: Uses a custom derive macro and bit-packing (not byte-aligned), so it is not wire-compatible with protobuf/flatbuffers/msgpack/capnp and has a smaller ecosystem/no cross-language schema story.
caveats: Numbers are from one dataset ('log') in a multi-dataset benchmark; other datasets in the same repo show different relative rankings. rustc flags beyond version/harness defaults are not spelled out.

name: postcard
workload: Serialize/deserialize of the 'log' dataset (small HTTP-request-log-like structs with many strings) in djkoloski/rust_serialization_benchmark.

name: rkyv
workload: Zero-copy access/read/update and serialize/deserialize of the 'log' dataset in djkoloski/rust_serialization_benchmark, compared against flatbuffers and capnp zero-copy access.
claimed_speedup: unvalidated zero-copy access 1.0907 ns vs flatbuffers unvalidated access 2.1807 ns (~2.0x); unvalidated read 8.3309 µs vs flatbuffers unvalidated read 42.209 µs (~5.1x); serialize 178.87 µs vs capnp 480.15 µs (~2.7x), flatbuffers 763.63 µs (~4.3x) (derived from page data)
compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.100.0-nightly (a36d05efa, 2026-09-09); criterion-based harness, exact opt-level flags not itemized beyond harness default
hardware: AMD EPYC 9V74 (2 cores / 4 threads visible to the VM), x86_64
tradeoffs: Zero-copy archived representation ties buffer layout to type layout/endianness; validated-access path (with error checking) is much slower than the unvalidated fast path shown here.
caveats: rkyv is already on the KNOWN_LIST; reported here only as better/fresher tier-A evidence (with stated CPU model and rustc version) than what may already be catalogued, per is_evidence_for_known=true.

name: protostuff
workload: Create/serialize/deserialize of the 'media content' object graph in the eishay/jvm-serializers 'staging' benchmark suite.
claimed_speedup: total time (create+serialize+deserialize) 1,173 µs vs protobuf 1,950 µs (~1.7x); serialize 444 µs vs protobuf 1,193 µs (~2.7x); deserialize 689 µs vs protobuf 689 µs (tie); wire size equal at 239 bytes (derived from page data)
tradeoffs: JVM-only; protostuff can emit protobuf-wire-compatible output while using a faster runtime encoder, but requires protostuff's own runtime schema/codegen machinery.
caveats: eishay/jvm-serializers wiki results page does not state JVM version, JVM flags, or CPU model, so capped at tier B despite being a very well-known, long-running independent suite; the parent repo itself has had no commits since 2023 (suite is stale, not the library).
